latestEpisode.description: This month we turn back the clock to 1977 to talk about the first expansion of the Lake Buena Vista Shopping Center, the Empress Lilly. The complex, which was designed to resemble an 1800's river boat, contained multiple restaurants and lounges, including a fine dining establishment which was the Victoria and Albert's of it's day. We'll discuss the building's interesting construction techniques, go over the menus items and prices at opening, and finally discuss that changes the facility went through before becoming Paddlefish today. latestEpisode.name: Final Bell: The Last AEW Unrestricted
latestEpisode.description:
AEW Unrestricted signs off with hosts Ref Aubrey Edwards and Will Washington reflecting on the moments, memories, and matches that defined the official podcast of All Elite Wrestling. They share behind-the-scenes stories from the show’s beginnings during the pandemic, how the podcast became a gateway for talent and fans alike, and what it meant to tell those stories week after week. Aubrey and Will shout out the people who made it all happen, including Tony Schiavone and Tony Khan, while revisiting favorite interviews, unforgettable episodes, and the impact Unrestricted had on AEW’s growth. Plus, they explain why now is the right time to close this chapter, what’s next for AEW podcasting, and why this isn’t goodbye...it’s just the end of this era.

Supreme Court Revives Trump Administration’s Voter Database
podcastProgress.description:
P.M. Edition for Sept. 25. The Supreme Court said today that Trump administration officials could use an expanded federal immigration database to check whether voters are citizens, which some states want to use to scrub voter rolls. Plus, the Ukraine war is stopping grain exports from getting out of the Black Sea, sending U.S. wheat futures to three-year highs. We hear from Journal reporter Alexander Osipovich about what the disruptions could mean for food prices and the global food supply. And a debut novel by Canadian-Haitian writer Thélyson Orélien was nominated for some of the top literary prizes in France… until accusations that the author used AI sparked controversy. Reporter Anna Silman discusses how the publishing world is handling the rise of AI. Alex Ossola hosts.

podcastProgress.trackName: Tisha Campbell
podcastProgress.description:
Tisha Campbell joins Shawn Stockman for a powerful and deeply personal episode of On That Note, reflecting on her legendary career in television, film, music, comedy, motherhood, and the journey of finally unmasking who she really is.

From her unforgettable roles as Gina Waters on Martin, Sydney in House Party, Yvonne in Boomerang, and Jay Kyle on My Wife and Kids, Tisha looks back at the moments that helped define her career and the cultural impact of Martin. She shares behind-the-scenes stories about working with Martin Lawrence, Tichina Arnold, Carl Anthony Payne II, Tommy Ford, Damon Wayans, Eddie Murphy, Robin Givens, Regina Hall, and the cast of Boomerang and House Party.

Tisha also opens up about her journey as a singer and R&B artist, including her time with Capitol Records, her music career during the height of Martin, and her song “Push.” She explains why she struggled to fully embrace her music career at the time and how acting ultimately became the path she believed could help her family.

The conversation takes an even more personal turn as Tisha discusses her childhood growing up in Newark, New Jersey, her family’s gospel music background, her mother and aunts singing alongside Mahalia Jackson, and how performing became part of her life at an early age. She shares the incredible story of winning a car in a childhood talent competition and booking her first acting role in The Magnificent Major.

Tisha also speaks candidly about autism, ADHD, masking, motherhood, therapy, and her son Zen, explaining how her own recent diagnosis helped her better understand herself and her experiences throughout her life. She discusses her book The A Word: A Mother and Son’s Journey Through Autism and Love, the importance of autism awareness, and how sharing her family’s journey online helped create a community around her son.

She also reveals the next chapter of her career as a writer, producer, and storyteller, including her production company You Go Girl Productions, her work with writing partner Danny Wright, her Lifetime project One Last Shot, and her desire to create stories that explore grief, family, healing, and the experiences of Black women.

Shawn and Tisha also revisit some of the most memorable moments from Martin, including the show’s iconic catchphrases, characters, comedy, and cultural impact that continues to reach new generations.

And in a revealing rapid-fire finale, Tisha talks about Gina vs. Jay, Sydney vs. Yvonne, acting vs. singing, comedy vs. drama, Martin Lawrence vs. Damon Wayans, Anita Baker, Meryl Streep, Amy Schumer, and the role she wishes more people knew about: Uncoupled.

podcastProgress.trackName: MVP Fires Back at the 22 Minute Hit Piece About His Show (EP. 73)
podcastProgress.description:
MVP holds Haters Court on Marking Out, putting a UK wrestling YouTuber's 22 minute hit piece on trial charge by charge. Marking Out with MVP & Dwayne Swayze is the weekly pro wrestling conversation between longtime friends Montel Vontavious Porter (MVP), a former WWE United States Champion and current AEW star and manager of The Hurt Syndicate, and Houston based rapper, songwriter, and recording artist Dwayne Swayze.

MVP opens the show wrecked after a brutal travel week off Collision in Charleston, West Virginia, driving to Huntington with Bobby Lashley to beat the Chicago storms and catching a 5 AM flight just to make the shoot. Then a quick tour of the speakeasy set and a Japanese whiskey pour before Dwayne calls the room to order.

Dwayne prosecutes nine charges from a critic who admits he barely watched the show. Main character syndrome, bought views, an anti Triple H agenda, no format, ugly thumbnails, green screen lighting, too much space between the hosts, the voice, and subscribers as a vanity metric. MVP answers each one with 25 years in the business behind him.

MVP and Swayze break down why subscribers and US audience percentage actually matter to sponsors, drop game for young wrestlers, and deliver a verdict. Closing out with MVP's "Spotlights" performance video featuring Baby Bash.

podcastProgress.trackName: 910: We Survived Halloween Horror Nights 35: Houses, Scare Zones & More
podcastProgress.description:
We’re stepping outside the Disney bubble and heading to Universal Orlando Resort for one of the biggest Halloween events of the year as we share our experience at Halloween Horror Nights 35!
We’re breaking down this year’s HHN from top to bottom, starting with the new Scream Early setup, how early entry works, when the houses begin opening, and what we think you need to know before planning your own night at the event.
Then we’re heading into the fog to talk about all 10 haunted houses. We’ll start with this year’s original concepts, including Jack & Oddfellow: Chaos & Control, H.R. Bloodengutz Presents: A Halloween Fright-Tacular!, MADLANDS: Caged Cannibals, Cybergoria, and INVASION: Alien Abduction. Then we’ll tackle the IP houses featuring Sinners, Stranger Things 5, Hellraiser, Evil Dead Burn, and Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness.
We’ll share what stood out inside each house, some of our favorite rooms and effects, which ones delivered the biggest scares, which concepts worked best for us, and where our experiences differed.
But HHN is about much more than the houses. We’re also exploring this year’s scare zones, including Infernal Carnival of Nightmares, Downtown Clowntown, Sideshow of Decay, and Fortnitemares, plus the Blood Noir: Echoes in the Fog nighttime show and the attractions you can experience during the event.
And after surviving all that, we’ll compare our favorites, biggest surprises, and overall impressions of HHN 35.
So grab your Scream Early ticket, head into the fog with us, and get ready for a night at Halloween Horror Nights!

Tommy Davidson joins Shawn Stockman for a powerful and hilarious conversation on a new episode of On That Note.

A legendary comedian, actor, impressionist, voice artist and original cast member of In Living Color, Tommy Davidson takes us behind the scenes of one of the most influential comedy shows in television history. Tommy reflects on working alongside Keenen Ivory Wayans, Jim Carrey, Damon Wayans, Jamie Foxx, David Alan Grier and the Wayans family, and explains what made In Living Color such a groundbreaking force in comedy and Black entertainment.

Tommy and Shawn also revisit the 1990s era of R&B and entertainment, discussing the incredible cultural moment that included Boyz II Men, Jodeci, Riff, Silk, Shai, SWV, TLC, Brownstone, Hi-Five and other legendary groups. The conversation explores the connection between music and comedy during that era and the impact those artists had on an entire generation.

The conversation takes a deeper turn as Tommy opens up about his extraordinary childhood and the circumstances surrounding his adoption. He shares the story of being abandoned as a baby in Mississippi, being rescued and adopted, growing up in Colorado and Wyoming, and eventually discovering his identity, his connection to Black culture and his passion for music and performance.

The two longtime friends revisit Tommy’s iconic Varnell Hill character from Martin and the incredible full-circle moment of bringing that character back more than 30 years later. Tommy discusses The Varnell Hill Show, his work as an executive producer alongside Martin Lawrence, and what it means to reinvent a character that audiences never forgot.

Tommy also discusses his film and television career, including Strictly Business, Booty Call, Ace Ventura: When Nature Calls, Bamboozled and his voice role as Oscar Proud on Disney’s The Proud Family.

From In Living Color and Martin to his new chapter with Varnell Hill, this is a conversation about comedy, music, Hollywood, survival, longevity, friendship, reinvention and the power of staying true to your gift.

Meta VR: Quest Gets a Glow-Up - Meta VR Glasses
podcastProgress.description:
Dan Moren of Six Colors joins the show this week! Meta's Muse has a zero-day vulnerability. Rat brains can power an AI model? Why are we hearing more about AI agents escaping their testing environments? And Meta's new VR glasses.
 
Dan talks about a new zero-day exploit that affects Meta's Muse AI agent, which allows an app or terminal command that can impersonate the AI agent and easily gain access to users' messages, emails, and other sensitive data. 
Mikah is amazed at the Biological Computing Company's new AI video model that was built from patterns utilizing lab-grown rat neurons. 
Mikah walks through The Verge's report on why researchers can't simply air-gap AI agents that keep escaping test environments and hitting real-world targets. 
And Scott Stein of CNET joins the show live from Meta's Headquarters to share his hands-on impressions of Meta's new VR glasses that were unveiled at this year's Meta Connect event.
